metadata.title: Quantum complexity theory
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json lists this paper as 'Simon, On the Power of Quantum Computation, 1994', but the PDF (paper318.txt) is actually Bernstein & Vazirani, 'Quantum complexity theory' (Sept 1997 manuscript / SIAM J. Comput. version of their STOC 1993 paper). Simon's paper is cited here as reference [39]. The pdf_source_url in metadata.json (theory.cs.berkeley.edu/~vazirani/pubs/bv.pdf) is consistent with Bernstein-Vazirani.
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced; some characters (especially angle brackets, epsilon, Hilbert space symbols, Dirac bra/ket) were garbled in OCR and reconstructed from context.

nodes.name: Quantum Turing Machine (QTM)
nodes.statement: A QTM $M = (\Sigma, Q, \delta)$ has finite alphabet $\Sigma$ with blank $\#$, finite state set $Q$ with start $q_0$ and final $q_f$, and quantum transition function $\delta: Q \times \Sigma \to \tilde{\mathbb{C}}^{\Sigma \times Q \times \{L,R\}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Modification of Deutsch's QTM definition: a probabilistic-TM-like device whose transition amplitudes are complex numbers from an efficiently computable subfield of C.

nodes.name: Well-formed QTM
nodes.statement: A QTM $M$ is well-formed if its time evolution operator $U_M$ preserves Euclidean length.
nodes.statement_clean: Well-formedness is the necessary condition for a QTM to be consistent with quantum physics.

nodes.name: Measurement of a QTM
nodes.statement: When QTM $M$ in superposition $\phi = \sum_i \alpha_i |c_i\rangle$ is observed, configuration $c_i$ is seen with probability $|\alpha_i|^2$ and the superposition collapses to $|c_i\rangle$. Partial measurements collapse to the consistent subspace, renormalized.

nodes.name: Simulation with slowdown
nodes.statement: QTM $M'$ simulates $M$ with slowdown $f$ and accuracy $\epsilon$ if observing $M'$ on input $x$ after $f(T)$ steps yields a distribution within total variation $\epsilon$ of observing $M$ on $x$ after $T$ steps.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-close QTMs
nodes.statement: QTMs $M$ and $M'$ are $\epsilon$-close if they share state set and alphabet and each pair of corresponding transition amplitudes differs in magnitude by at most $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Final configuration / halting / polynomial-time QTM
nodes.statement: A final configuration is one in state $q_f$. $M$ halts at time $T$ on input $x$ if the time-$T$ superposition consists entirely of final configurations and no earlier superposition contains any. A polynomial-time QTM is well-formed and halts in time polynomial in $|x|$.

nodes.name: Well-behaved / stationary QTM
nodes.statement: A QTM is well-behaved if it halts on every input in a final superposition where each configuration has the tape head in the same cell. It is stationary if that cell is the start cell.

nodes.name: Normal form QTM
nodes.statement: A QTM (or deterministic TM) $M = (\Sigma, Q, \delta)$ is in normal form if $\forall \sigma \in \Sigma:\; \delta(q_f, \sigma) = |\sigma\rangle |q_0\rangle |R\rangle$.

nodes.name: Unidirectional QTM
nodes.statement: QTM $M$ is unidirectional if each state can be entered from only one direction: whenever $\delta(p_1, \sigma_1, \tau_1, q, d_1)$ and $\delta(p_2, \sigma_2, \tau_2, q, d_2)$ are both nonzero, $d_1 = d_2$.

nodes.name: Multi-track TM
nodes.statement: A TM with $k$ tracks has alphabet $\Sigma_1 \times \cdots \times \Sigma_k$ with per-track blank symbol $\#$. Inputs and head alignments are specified per track.

nodes.name: Reversible Turing Machine
nodes.statement: A reversible TM is a deterministic TM in which each configuration has at most one predecessor (single tape, head moves in $\{L,R\}$, $\delta$ a total function).

nodes.name: Restricted update superposition (direction $d$-going)
nodes.statement: $\delta(p, \sigma | \tau, d)$ is the superposition of states obtained from $\delta(p, \sigma)$ by restricting to transitions writing symbol $\tau$ and moving in direction $d$.

nodes.name: Partial / well-formed partial QTM
nodes.statement: A partial QTM has $\delta$ defined only on a subset $S \subseteq Q \times \Sigma$. It is well-formed if its defined entries satisfy unit length, orthogonality, and separability.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-close to unitary
nodes.statement: A bounded operator $U$ is $\epsilon$-close to unitary if there exists a unitary $\tilde{U}$ with $\|U - \tilde{U}\| \le \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Near-trivial unitary matrix
nodes.statement: A $d \times d$ unitary $M$ is near-trivial if either (i) it is the identity except a single diagonal entry equals $e^{i\theta}$ (phase shift), or (ii) it is the identity except for a $2 \times 2$ rotation block in dimensions $j, k$ by angle $\theta$.

nodes.name: QTM carries out a transformation
nodes.statement: Encoding $x_U$ causes $M$ to carry out the $k$-cell transformation $U$ with accuracy $\epsilon$ in time $T$ if for every $|\phi\rangle$, on input $|\phi\rangle |x_U\rangle |\eta\rangle$, $M$ halts in $T$ steps with final superposition $(U' |\phi\rangle) |x\rangle$ where $U'$ is unitary and $\|U - U'\| \le \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Formal definition of what it means for a QTM to implement a specified linear transformation up to accuracy $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Oracle QTM
nodes.statement: A QTM with a query track and distinguished pre-query state $q_q$ and post-query state $q_a$. Entering $q_q$ with query-track contents $|x \cdot b\rangle$ causes the oracle to update it to $|x \cdot (b \oplus f(x))\rangle$ and switch control to $q_a$.

nodes.name: Acceptance, EQP, BQP, BQTime
nodes.statement: QTM $M$ accepts $x$ with probability $p$ if observing the start cell of the last track shows 1 with probability $p$. EQP is the class exactly accepted by polynomial-time QTMs; BQP is the class accepted with probability $\ge 2/3$ by polynomial-time QTMs. BQTime$(T(n))$ generalizes BQP to bound $T(n)$.

nodes.name: Fourier sampling problem
nodes.statement: Given a function $f: \mathbb{Z}_2^n \to \mathbb{C}$ of unit norm (e.g. $f(x) = g(x)/2^{n/2}$ for $g: \mathbb{Z}_2^n \to \{-1,1\}$), sample $s \in \mathbb{Z}_2^n$ from the distribution $P[s] = |\hat{f}(s)|^2$ where $\hat{f}$ is the discrete Fourier (Hadamard) transform of $f$.

nodes.name: Recursive Fourier sampling / language $R^O$
nodes.statement: For each candidate $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ (with $n$ a power of 2), build a recursive tree where a node at level $l$ has $2^{2^l}$ children. A legal oracle $O$ assigns a value $V_O$ at each node by recursive parity. The language $R^O$ contains those candidates with $V_O(x) = 1$.

nodes.name: Hit / fixed-by-constraint / run
nodes.statement: For a node $x$ at level $l \ge 0$ with $k_x$ such that $V_O(x \$ y) = (-1)^{y \cdot k_x}$, the query $x \$ k_x$ is a hit. A run of size $k$ is a pair $(S, f)$ with $|S| = k$ query strings and $f: S \to \{0,1\}$ such that some legal oracle agrees with $f$.

nodes.name: Efficiently computable amplitudes $\tilde{\mathbb{C}}$
nodes.statement: $\tilde{\mathbb{C}}$ is the set of $\alpha \in \mathbb{C}$ for which there is a deterministic algorithm computing $\mathrm{Re}(\alpha)$ and $\mathrm{Im}(\alpha)$ to within $2^{-n}$ in time polynomial in $n$. QTM transition amplitudes are required to lie in $\tilde{\mathbb{C}}$.

nodes.name: Variation distance from Euclidean distance
nodes.statement: Let $\phi, \psi \in S$ with $\|\phi\| = \|\psi\| = 1$ and $\|\phi - \psi\| \le \epsilon$. Then the total variation distance between the measurement distributions of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is at most $4\epsilon$.
conclusions: Total variation distance between measurement distributions $\le 4\epsilon$

nodes.name: Linear error accumulation
nodes.statement: Let $U$ be the time evolution of QTM $M$ and $T > 0$. If $|\phi_0\rangle, |\tilde{\phi}_0\rangle, \ldots, |\phi_T\rangle, |\tilde{\phi}_T\rangle$ satisfy $\||\phi_i\rangle - |\tilde{\phi}_i\rangle\| \le \epsilon$ and $|\phi_i\rangle = U|\tilde{\phi}_{i-1}\rangle$, then $\||\tilde{\phi}_T\rangle - U^T |\phi_0\rangle\| \le T\epsilon$.
assumptions: $U$ is the time evolution of well-formed QTM $M$

nodes.name: Time-evolution closeness from amplitude closeness
nodes.statement: If QTMs $M$ and $M'$ with alphabet $\Sigma$ and state set $Q$ are $\epsilon$-close, then $\|U - U'\| \le 2\,\mathrm{card}(\Sigma)\,\mathrm{card}(Q)\,\epsilon$. Holds even if $M$ or $M'$ is not well-formed.
assumptions: $M$ and $M'$ are $\epsilon$-close QTMs with alphabet $\Sigma$ and state set $Q$

nodes.name: $O(\log T)$ bits of precision suffice
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a well-formed QTM and $M'$ a QTM that is $\frac{\epsilon}{24\,\mathrm{card}(\Sigma)\,\mathrm{card}(Q)\,T}$-close to $M$, with $\epsilon > 0$. Then $M'$ simulates $M$ for $T$ steps with accuracy $\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Synchronization Theorem
nodes.statement: If $f: \Sigma^* \to \Sigma^*$ is computable in deterministic polynomial time and $|f(x)|$ depends only on $|x|$, then there is a polynomial-time, stationary, normal-form reversible TM that on input $x$ outputs $x; f(x)$ with running time depending only on $|x|$. If $f$ is one-to-one with $f$ and $f^{-1}$ both poly-time computable, the same holds for output $f(x)$ alone.
assumptions: $f$ is computable in deterministic polynomial time
conclusions: There is a polynomial-time stationary normal-form reversible TM that on input $x$ outputs $x; f(x)$
Its running time depends only on $|x|$

nodes.name: Reversible TMs are well-formed QTMs
nodes.statement: Any reversible TM is also a well-formed QTM.

nodes.name: Adding a passive track
nodes.statement: Given any QTM (reversible TM) $M = (\Sigma, Q, \delta)$ and any set $\Sigma'$, there is a QTM (reversible TM) $M' = (\Sigma \times \Sigma', Q, \delta')$ that behaves exactly as $M$ while leaving its second track unchanged.

nodes.name: Track permutation
nodes.statement: Given a QTM (reversible TM) $M$ on $\Sigma_1 \times \cdots \times \Sigma_k$ and a permutation $\pi$ on $[1,k]$, there is a QTM (reversible TM) $M'$ on the permuted alphabet that behaves as $M$ with tracks permuted by $\pi$.

nodes.name: Swapping transitions preserves well-formedness
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a well-formed QTM (reversible TM), then swapping the incoming or outgoing transitions between any pair of states gives another well-formed QTM (reversible TM).

nodes.name: Union of well-formed QTMs
nodes.statement: If $M_1 = (\Sigma, Q_1, \delta_1)$ and $M_2 = (\Sigma, Q_2, \delta_2)$ are well-formed QTMs (reversible TMs) with disjoint state sets, then $M = (\Sigma, Q_1 \cup Q_2, \delta_1 \cup \delta_2)$ with any chosen start state in $Q_1 \cup Q_2$ is also well-formed.

nodes.name: State-insertion lemma
nodes.statement: If $M_1, M_2$ are normal-form QTMs (reversible TMs) with the same alphabet and $q$ is a state of $M_1$, then there is a normal-form QTM $M$ that acts as $M_1$ except each visit to $q$ runs $M_2$ instead.

nodes.name: Dovetailing Lemma
nodes.statement: If $M_1$ and $M_2$ are well-behaved, normal-form QTMs (reversible TMs) with the same alphabet, then there is a normal-form QTM (reversible TM) $M$ which carries out $M_1$ followed by $M_2$.
assumptions: $M_1, M_2$ are well-behaved, normal-form QTMs/reversible TMs with same alphabet
conclusions: There exists a normal-form $M$ executing $M_1$ then $M_2$

nodes.name: Branching Lemma
nodes.statement: If $M_1, M_2$ are well-behaved, normal-form QTMs with the same alphabet, there is a well-behaved, normal-form QTM $M$ that, depending on a control bit on track 2, runs $M_1$ or $M_2$ on track 1, taking exactly four extra steps.

nodes.name: Reverses a computation
nodes.statement: QTM $M_2$ reverses $M_1$ if for every input $x$ on which $M_1$ halts, with $c_x$ initial and $\phi_x$ final superposition of $M_1$, $M_2$ halts on $\phi_x$ with final superposition $|c_x\rangle$ (initial/final states of $M_1$ identified with final/initial of $M_2$).

nodes.name: Reversal Lemma
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a normal-form, reversible TM or unidirectional QTM then there is a normal-form reversible TM or QTM $M'$ that reverses the computation of $M$ while taking two extra time steps.
assumptions: $M$ is a normal-form, unidirectional QTM (or reversible TM)
conclusions: There exists $M'$ in normal form that reverses $M$ with two extra time steps

nodes.name: Looping Lemma
nodes.statement: There is a stationary, normal-form, reversible TM $M$ and constant $c$ such that on input positive integer $k$ in binary, $M$ runs for time $O(k \log^c k)$, halts with tape unchanged, and has a state $q^*$ visited exactly $k$ times with the head in the start cell.

nodes.name: Change of basis preserves well-formedness
nodes.statement: Given QTM $M = (\Sigma, Q, \delta)$ and an orthonormal basis $B \subset \tilde{\mathbb{C}}^Q$ for $\mathbb{C}^Q$, there is a QTM $M' = (\Sigma, B, \delta')$ that evolves exactly as $M$ under the change of basis from $Q$ to $B$.

nodes.name: Local conditions for QTM well-formedness
nodes.statement: QTM $M = (\Sigma, Q, \delta)$ is well-formed iff: (i) Unit length $\|\delta(p, \sigma)\| = 1$ for all $(p, \sigma)$; (ii) Orthogonality $\delta(p_1, \sigma_1) \cdot \delta(p_2, \sigma_2) = 0$ for distinct pairs; (iii) Separability $\delta(p_1, \sigma_1 | \tau_1, L) \cdot \delta(p_2, \sigma_2 | \tau_2, R) = 0$.
conclusions: $M$ is well-formed iff Unit length, Orthogonality, and Separability all hold

nodes.name: Interleaving lemma
nodes.statement: Given $k$ state sets $Q_0, \ldots, Q_{k-1}, Q_k = Q_0$ and length-preserving transition functions $\delta_i: Q_i \times \Sigma \to \tilde{\mathbb{C}}^{\Sigma \times Q_{i+1} \times \{L,R\}}$, there is a well-formed QTM $M$ with state set $\bigcup_i (Q_i, i)$ that alternates stepping according to each $\delta_i$.

nodes.name: Unidirection Lemma
nodes.statement: Any QTM $M$ is simulated, with slowdown by a factor of 5, by a unidirectional QTM $M'$. If $M$ is well-behaved and in normal form, so is $M'$.
conclusions: $M$ is simulated with slowdown 5 by a unidirectional QTM $M'$

nodes.name: Completion Lemma
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a well-formed partial QTM with transition function $\delta$, there is a well-formed QTM $M'$ with the same state set and alphabet whose transition function $\delta'$ agrees with $\delta$ wherever the latter is defined.

nodes.name: Norm bounds for matrices close to unitary
nodes.statement: If a $d$-dimensional complex matrix $M$ is $\epsilon$-close to unitary, then $1 - \epsilon \le \|M_i\| \le 1 + \epsilon$, and for $i \ne j$, $\|M_i M_j^*\| \le 2\epsilon + 3\epsilon^2$.

nodes.name: Small-entry implies small-norm
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a $d$-dimensional square complex matrix with $|m_{i,j}| \le \epsilon$ for all $i, j$, then $\|M\| \le d\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Vector-rotation algorithm via near-trivial matrices
nodes.statement: There is a deterministic algorithm that on input $v \in \mathbb{C}^d$ and $\epsilon > 0$ computes near-trivial matrices $U_1, \ldots, U_{2d-1}$ with $\|U_1 \cdots U_{2d-1} v - \|v\| e_1\| \le \epsilon$, in time poly($d, \log(1/\epsilon)$, $|v|$).

nodes.name: Unitary decomposition into near-trivial matrices
nodes.statement: There is a deterministic algorithm running in time poly($d, \log(1/\epsilon)$, input length) which on input $U, \epsilon$ with $U$ a $d \times d$ matrix $\frac{\epsilon}{2(10\sqrt{d})^d}$-close to unitary, computes $d$-dimensional near-trivial matrices $U_1, \ldots, U_n$ with $n$ polynomial in $d$ such that $\|U - U_n \cdots U_1\| \le \epsilon$.
conclusions: Near-trivial $U_1, \ldots, U_n$ with $n$ polynomial in $d$ exist with $\|U - U_n \cdots U_1\| \le \epsilon$

nodes.name: Approximating arbitrary rotation by multiples of fixed angle $R$
nodes.statement: Let $R = 2\pi \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} 2^{-2^i}$. There is a deterministic poly-time algorithm that on input $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ and $\epsilon > 0$ produces an integer $k$ polynomial in $1/\epsilon$ with $|kR - \theta| \bmod 2\pi \le \epsilon$.

nodes.name: QTM carrying out near-trivial transformations
nodes.statement: There is a stationary, normal-form QTM $M$ with first-track alphabet $\{\#, 0, 1\}$ that carries out the set of near-trivial transformations on its first track in polynomial time.

nodes.name: Unitary Transformation Theorem
nodes.statement: There is a stationary, normal-form QTM $M$ with first-track alphabet $\{\#, 0, 1\}$ that carries out all transformations on its first track in polynomial time, with required closeness factor $\frac{1}{2(10\sqrt{d})^d}$ for transformations of dimension $d$.
assumptions: Input is dimension-$d$ matrix $U$ that is $\frac{\epsilon}{2(10\sqrt{d})^d}$-close to unitary
conclusions: Stationary normal-form QTM applies an $\epsilon$-approximation of $U$ on the first $\log d$ cells

nodes.name: Efficient universal QTM
nodes.statement: There is a normal-form QTM $\mathcal{M}$ such that for any well-formed QTM $M$, $\epsilon > 0$, and $T$, $\mathcal{M}$ simulates $M$ with accuracy $\epsilon$ for $T$ steps with slowdown polynomial in $T$ and $1/\epsilon$.
conclusions: There is a fixed normal-form QTM $\mathcal{M}$ simulating $M$ for $T$ steps with accuracy $\epsilon$

nodes.name: $\mathrm{P} \subseteq \mathrm{EQP}$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{P} \subseteq \mathrm{EQP}$.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{BPP} \subseteq \mathrm{BQP}$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{BPP} \subseteq \mathrm{BQP}$.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{BQP} \subseteq \mathrm{PSPACE}$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{BQP} \subseteq \mathrm{PSPACE}$.

nodes.name: Clean BQP machine (amplification)
nodes.statement: If $L \in \mathrm{BQTime}(T(n))$ with $T(n) > n$ time-constructible, then for any $\epsilon > 0$ there is a QTM $M'$ that accepts $L$ with probability $1 - \epsilon$, runs in time $cT(n)$ where $c$ is poly in $\log(1/\epsilon)$, and produces a final superposition with squared magnitude at least $1 - \epsilon$ on $|x\rangle |L(x)\rangle$.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{BQP} \subseteq \mathrm{P}^{\#\mathrm{P}}$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{BQP} \subseteq \mathrm{P}^{\#\mathrm{P}}$.

nodes.name: Reversal of an oracle QTM
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a normal-form, unidirectional oracle QTM then there is a normal-form oracle QTM $M'$ such that for any oracle $O$, $M'^O$ reverses the computation of $M^O$ in two extra time steps.

nodes.name: Hadamard transform QTM
nodes.statement: There is a normal-form QTM that on initial superposition of $n$-bit strings $|\phi\rangle$ halts in $2n + 4$ steps with the head back in the start cell and produces $H_n |\phi\rangle$ where $H_n$ is the Hadamard transform.

nodes.name: Fourier sampling with respect to $g$
nodes.statement: For every polynomial-time computable $g: \{0,1\}^n \to \{-1, 1\}$, there is a polynomial-time stationary QTM that on input $0^n$ produces, when its final superposition is observed, each $n$-bit string $s$ with probability $|\hat{f}(s)|^2$ where $f(x) = g(x)/2^{n/2}$.
conclusions: There is a polynomial-time stationary QTM that samples from $|\hat{f}(s)|^2$

nodes.name: Recursive Fourier sampling is in BQP (with oracle)
nodes.statement: There is an oracle QTM $M$ such that for every legal oracle $O$, $M^O$ runs in polynomial time and accepts the language $R^O$ with probability 1.
conclusions: $M^O$ accepts $R^O$ with probability 1 in polynomial time

nodes.name: Hit-probability bound across ancestor
nodes.statement: For run $r$, ancestor $x$ of node $y$: $P_x(y) \le 2 P(y)$.

nodes.name: Inductive bound on hit probability
nodes.statement: If $r$ is a run, $y$ a node at level $l \ge 2$ with $q$ queries from $r$ at or below $y$, and $x$ an ancestor of $y$, then $P_x(y) \le q / \beta(n/4)$ where $n = 2^l$ and $\beta(n) = n^{(n/2) - 1}$.
assumptions: $r$ a run; $y$ at level $l \ge 2$ with $q$ queries at or below $y$

nodes.name: Recursive Fourier sampling lower bound vs BPP
nodes.statement: For any $T(n) = n^{o(\log n)}$, relative to a random legal oracle $O$, with probability 1, $R^O$ is not contained in $\mathrm{BPTime}(T(n))^O$.
conclusions: Relative to random legal oracle, $R^O \notin \mathrm{BPTime}(T(n))$ with probability 1

nodes.name: QTM is well-formed iff time evolution is unitary
nodes.statement: A QTM is well-formed iff its time evolution operator is unitary.
conclusions: $M$ well-formed $\Leftrightarrow$ time evolution operator $U_M$ is unitary

nodes.name: Reversibility characterization
nodes.statement: A TM (or generalized TM) $M$ is reversible iff (1) each state can be entered while moving in only one direction, and (2) the transition function $\delta$ is one-to-one when direction is ignored.
conclusions: $M$ is reversible iff (one-direction entry) AND (one-to-one $\delta$ ignoring direction)

nodes.name: Each configuration has exactly one predecessor
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a reversible TM then every configuration of $M$ has exactly one predecessor.

nodes.name: Completion of partial reversible $\delta$
nodes.statement: If $\delta$ is a partial function $Q \times \Sigma \to \Sigma \times Q \times \{L,R\}$ satisfying the two conditions of the reversibility characterization, then $\delta$ extends to a total function still satisfying those conditions.

nodes.name: Generalized reversible TMs simulated with slowdown 2
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a generalized reversible TM then there is a reversible TM $M'$ that simulates $M$ with slowdown at most 2.

nodes.name: String-exchange reversible TM
nodes.statement: For any $\Sigma$, there is a normal-form reversible TM with alphabet $\Sigma \times \Sigma$ that on input $x; y$ runs for $2 \max(|x|, |y|) + 4$ steps and outputs $y; x$.

nodes.name: String-copying reversible TM
nodes.statement: For any $\Sigma$, there is a normal-form reversible TM with alphabet $\Sigma \times \Sigma$ that on input $x$ outputs $x; x$ and on input $x; x$ outputs $x$, in $2|x| + 4$ steps.

nodes.name: Reversible simulation of oblivious deterministic TMs
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be an oblivious deterministic TM producing output $M(x)$ with the head back in the start cell. Then there is a reversible TM $M'$ that on input $x$ produces $x; M(x)$ and on input $x; M(x)$ produces $x$, with running time depending only on $|x|$ and $|M(x)|$ and bounded by a quadratic polynomial in $M$'s running time.

nodes.name: Reversible computation of one-to-one functions
nodes.statement: Let $M_1$ be an oblivious TM with $|M_1(x)|$ depending only on $|x|$ and $M_2$ an oblivious TM that inverts $M_1$. Then there is a reversible TM $M'$ that on input $x$ outputs $M_1(x)$, with running time depending only on $|x|$.

nodes.name: Map-vector-to-axis algorithm (near-trivial decomposition of a vector)
nodes.statement: Iterative algorithm computing near-trivial matrices $U_1, \ldots, U_{2d-1}$ that map a given vector $v$ to (approximately) $\|v\| e_1$ via $d$ phase shifts followed by $d-1$ rotations.
output: Near-trivial matrices $U_1, \ldots, U_{2d-1}$ with $\|U_1 \cdots U_{2d-1} v - \|v\| e_1\| \le \epsilon$

nodes.name: Decompose-unitary algorithm (into near-trivial matrices)
nodes.statement: Algorithm that approximates a $d \times d$ matrix $U$ close to unitary by a polynomial-length product of near-trivial matrices, by sequentially zeroing out rows and columns using AP318.1.
input: $d \times d$ matrix $U$ that is $\frac{\epsilon}{2(10\sqrt{d})^d}$-close to unitary
output: Near-trivial matrices $U_1, \ldots, U_n$ with $n$ polynomial in $d$

nodes.name: Universal QTM simulation procedure (STEP)
nodes.statement: Procedure executed once per simulated step inside the universal QTM: transfer current state/symbol to workspace, apply unitary $U$ to within $\epsilon$, restore the cell, and shift the new state one supercell in the direction encoded by string $s$.
input: Encoding of unidirectional QTM $M'$ (alphabet, states, transition function specification)
Simulation tape supercell representation of current configuration
output: Updated supercell representation after one step of $M'$
Tape head returned to start cell
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Transfer (p, sigma) to workspace, leaving marker.  2. Apply U to (p, sigma) to within eta, producing superposition over (q, tau).  3. Reverse Step 1, returning (q, tau) to the marked supercell.  4. Shift state spec q one supercell left or right per s[q].

nodes.name: Universal QTM (full procedure)
nodes.statement: Algorithm that converts an arbitrary input QTM $M$ to a unidirectional $M'$ via the Unidirection Lemma, encodes its supercell representation, and iterates STEP $5T$ times via the Looping Lemma.
input: Specification of QTM $M$ (alphabets, states, transition algorithm)
output: Final superposition within total variation $\epsilon$ of $M$ on $x$ at time $T$

nodes.name: Fourier sampling QTM (5-step procedure)
nodes.statement: Five-step QTM procedure: (1) Hadamard on $0^n$, (2) compute $f$, (3) phase by $f(i)$, (4) reverse step 2, (5) Hadamard.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Apply Hadamard to 0^n -> uniform superposition over i.  2. Compute f to produce |i>|f(i)>.  3. Apply phase f(i) to each |i>.  4. Reverse Step 2 to erase f(i).  5. Apply Hadamard, then measure.

nodes.name: Recursive Fourier sampling QTM
nodes.statement: Recursive quantum algorithm computing $V_O(x)$: split into superposition of children, recursively compute $V_O$ of children, apply phases, reverse, Hadamard to get $k_x$, query $O(x \$ k_x)$, then reverse to clean up.
nodes.pseudocode: If x leaf: query O(x). Else (level l>=1):  1. Equal superposition over 2^{2^l} children.  2. Recursively compute V_O for children.  3. Apply phase V_O(child) to each.  4. Reverse Step 2.  5. Apply Hadamard -> superposition collapses to k_x.  6. Query x$k_x to get V_O(x).  7. Reverse Steps 1-5.

nodes.name: Norm-preservation equivalence
nodes.statement: $\forall x \in V:\; \|Ux\| = \|x\| \;\Leftrightarrow\; \forall x, y \in V:\; (Ux, Uy) = (x, y)$.

nodes.name: Composition error bound for unitary approximations
Discrete Fourier transform / Hadamard basis identity
nodes.statement: For $f: \mathbb{Z}_2^n \to \mathbb{C}$, $f = \sum_s \hat{f}(s) \chi_s$ with $\hat{f}(s) = (f, \chi_s)$ and $\chi_s(x) = 2^{-n/2} (-1)^{s \cdot x}$. Parseval: $\sum_x |f(x)|^2 = \sum_s |\hat{f}(s)|^2$.

nodes.name: $O(\log T)$ precision sufficiency (vs $O(T)$)
nodes.statement: QTM transition amplitudes need only $O(\log T)$ bits of precision to support $T$ steps of computation with bounded accuracy. Lipton observed that the relevant measure is one part in $T^{O(1)}$, not $T^{O(1)}$ bits.

nodes.name: Three rationals suffice for amplitudes
nodes.statement: Adleman-DeMarrais-Huang and Solovay-Yao showed that amplitudes from $\{0, \pm 3/5, \pm 4/5, \pm 1\}$ suffice to construct a universal QTM.

nodes.name: BQP sandwiched between BPP and P^#P
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{BPP} \subseteq \mathrm{BQP} \subseteq \mathrm{P}^{\#\mathrm{P}}$, so any unrelativized proof that $\mathrm{BQP} \ne \mathrm{BPP}$ would imply a major separation in classical complexity.

nodes.name: Polylogarithmic-slowdown universal QTM
nodes.statement: Conjecture: with more care, a universal QTM can be constructed whose slowdown is only polylogarithmic in $T$ rather than linear in $T$.

nodes.name: Quantum cellular automata vs QTMs
nodes.statement: It is open whether quantum cellular automata can be more powerful than quantum Turing machines (modulo the question of the correct definition of a quantum cellular automaton).

nodes.name: Simon's oracle separation (cited)
nodes.statement: There is an oracle relative to which a certain problem can be solved in polynomial time on a QTM but cannot be solved in less than $2^{n/2}$ steps on a probabilistic Turing machine; the problem is in $\mathrm{NP} \cap \mathrm{co\text{-}NP}$.
nodes.origin_citation: Simon 1994, On the power of quantum computation

nodes.name: Shor's factoring/discrete-log algorithm (cited)
nodes.statement: There exist polynomial-time quantum algorithms for the integer factoring and discrete logarithm problems.
nodes.origin_citation: Shor 1994, Algorithms for quantum computation: discrete log and factoring

nodes.name: Bennett's reversible simulation (cited)
nodes.statement: Any deterministic Turing machine can be efficiently simulated by a reversible Turing machine; quantum computers are at least as powerful as classical computers.

nodes.name: Deutsch's universal QTM (cited)
nodes.statement: Universal quantum Turing machine construction with simulation overhead exponential in $T$.
nodes.origin_citation: Deutsch 1985, Quantum theory, the Church-Turing principle and the universal quantum computer
